messages:
Alex: Heads-up — followup from RFC #312 about the fingerprint shim migration. Can we sync on the remaining decisions and rollout playbook?
Mira: yes — main open decisions: client-side header vs service-generated fingerprint, how to handle late-arrival tokens, and auditability for billing.
Sam: my preference is client header + server canonicalizer. client header reduces compute on our edge but we need a strict proto and a validator.
Irene: +1 to client header for first pass, but we must treat headers as advisory. service must still generate on ingest and attach canonical id before ledger append. otherwise we risk double counting during mismatch windows.
Alex: agreed — so migration plan: 1) accept client header (v1) and record it, 2) parallel-generate server fingerprint and store both, 3) run reconciliation job for X days and emit drift metrics.
Mira: reconciliation window length? RFC suggested 7 days, but with late-arrival patterns we may need 14. also need SLA impact estimate for billing pipeline (qps/CPU).
Sam: 14 days seems safer. I'll run a load estimate: generating fingerprint is ~8ms per request in Python baseline, C++ optimized path ~1.2ms. with current qps that’s ~120 cores vs 18 cores. we should enable optimized kernel earlier or do sampling.
Irene: Sampling for production verification: sample 5% of traffic to do both fingerprint paths today, gradually increase to 100% by canary. That reduces CPU while we validate.
Alex: what about late-arrivals and watermarking? We can't just drop corrections after 7d window — billing must be correct.
Mira: proposal: keep an append-only corrections table that reconciler can write to. Billing job consumes canonical ledger + corrections stream. corrections are idempotent deltas (credit/debit). TTL for corrections = 90 days.
Sam: idempotency key should be the canonical fingerprint + event-seq. Also need a provenance pointer to original request (for audits).
Irene: For audits we should store: original client header (if any), server fingerprint, model-version, route, token-count, and ingest-timestamp. Keep minimal PII.
Alex: agreed. Also add a 'fingerprint_v' field so we can upgrade proto without ambiguity.
Mira: ops: rollout stages: dev -> shadow (5%) -> canary (20%) -> full. each stage runs the reconciler in dry-run and emits two metrics: drift_rate and billing_delta_rate. threshold for promotion: drift_rate < 0.1% and billing_delta_rate < 0.05%.
Sam: edge-case: clients that garbage-header fingerprint. We should validate checksum prefix (sha256 hex, 16 chars) and reject obviously malformed. Log to sampling bucket for partner outreach.
Irene: backlog item: add negative-case enrichment to audit UI so support can inspect mismatched pairs quickly.
Alex: migration backfill: we will run a historical canonicalizer on last 30 days of raw events to generate server fingerprints, then run billing-recon to find net diffs. plan to apply corrections incrementally over 2 weeks to avoid invoice shocks.
Mira: is there an orchestration plan for backfill? we need rate limits and replay isolation so it doesn’t affect realtime ingestion.
Sam: run backfill via offline job in k8s batch cluster using a sharded windowed reader. throttle to 40% of cluster capacity. replay writes to corrections topic, not main ledger.
Irene: add test harness: a small sim that replays synthetic late-arrival and duplicate messages to validate the reconciler logic. I can prototype it.
Alex: security question: storing original headers — do we need encryption at rest for that field?
Mira: yes. treat original headers as potentially sensitive; encrypt with KMS and redact in UI. store only fingerprint cleartext.
Sam: what about cost visibility? Redwood Console needs to show both pre- and post-reconciled token tallies for a billing window. customers will ask why numbers changed.
Irene: UX: surface a ‘reconciliation delta’ line item on invoices with a link to the audit trace. We should keep deltas grouped by cause (late-arrival, dedupe, fingerprint-mismatch).
Alex: can we make reconciliation deterministic so that re-running the same backfill doesn't flip numbers? i.e., corrections must be idempotent and monotonic.
Sam: yes — corrections are signed with the reconciliation-run-id and written as upserts to a corrections ledger keyed by (canonical_fingerprint, billing_window). reconciliation-run-id monotonic ensures last-write-wins but we prefer append-only signed corrections and reconciliation selects max(seq).
Mira: ops/alerts: create an SLO on drift_rate and generate alerts when drift_rate spikes above 0.5% in a 1h window.
Irene: deploy-bot: rolling out the ingest-side validator patch to staging now.
deploy-bot: rollout started: metering-ingest-validator v2 -> staging (pods: 3 -> 3). logs: tail: kubectl -n prod logs -f deploy/metering-validator
Sam: nice. once in staging I'll run the sim harness and post results.
Alex: next steps: Sam to produce cost/cpu estimate + sampling plan by EOD Fri; Irene to prototype sim and audit UI mock; Mira to draft rollout doc with thresholds and backfill mechanics. we'll reconvene Tue.
Mira: tagging @support-team FYI for UI/backfill customer comms. :eyes:
Irene: noted. I'll add a quick runbook for support with common queries and trace examples.
Alex: thanks all — closing checkin.
